title: Autoscaler horizon misprojection causing underprovisioned tenant headroom during promo traffic
creator: Nina Patel
description:
Summary: Several Dedicated customers experienced sudden token throttling and 429s during scheduled promotional traffic spikes. The autoscaler underprovisioned reserved pool headroom because the lookahead/horizon estimator consistently predicted demand below actuals for short-lived, high-amplitude ramps. This ticket tracks investigation, a targeted hotfix, rollout plan, telemetry additions, and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.

Observed symptoms: multiple tenants in us-west-2 reported elevated latency and 429s between 2026-02-18T15:30 and 2026-02-18T17:00 UTC during marketing-driven traffic bursts. Autoscaler logs show scale decisions were suppressed by the projection module which returned a 30% lower demand forecast compared to arrival rates. Manual scale-up interventions restored headroom.

Root cause hypothesis: the autoscaler uses an exponential weighted moving average (EWMA) combined with an arrival-rate derivative estimator and an internal "horizon" (lookahead window). For very sharp ramps, the EWMA's smoothing plus a legacy clamp in the horizon calculation biased the projection downward when the short-term variance exceeded an internal threshold. Additionally, a recent optimization (ENG-439210) that minimized oscillation by extending cooldowns inadvertently extended the window used by the projection, delaying scale decisions. Together these changes caused the system to underpredict transient promos.

Fix implemented: 1) Replace the horizon clamp with a demand-adaptive Poisson arrival estimator that uses recent arrival bursts to weight the lookahead. 2) Introduce a minimum short-term multiplier for the projection when variance spikes are detected (prevents aggressive smoothing). 3) Reduce cooldown extension when the projection crosses a high-variance threshold. 4) Add unit tests and an integration test harness that replays promo-like traffic patterns.

Mitigations applied: a) Emergency manual headroom top-up for affected tenants on 2026-02-18. b) Hotfix branch created and canaried to dev and then to us-west-2 dedicated pool on 2026-02-19. c) Temporary conservative cap removal on burst throttling rules for tiered tenants to reduce false-positive 429s.

Monitoring and observability added: new dashboard panels for projection_error_ratio, short_term_variance, cooling_extension_seconds, and per-tenant headroom_gap. Alerts: projection_error_ratio > 0.25 for 5m triggers paging and automatic conservative scale-up on a 10% headroom target.

Next steps: finish integration test coverage, complete rollout to remaining regions, backport safe fix to runtime-1.20 if requested by customers, document algorithm trade-offs in the Console runbook, and schedule a postmortem with affected customers and SRE.
